edition.editorialNote: Devanāgarī and IAST saṃhitā follow the public-domain GRETIL and SanskritDocuments witnesses, cross-checked letter-by-letter. The English rendering is Charles Johnston's 1912 public-domain interpretation. See the Sources view for links, hashes, and the numbering note for YS 3.22.

translation.text: OM: Here follows Instruction in Union.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Union, spiritual consciousness, is gained through control of the versatile psychic nature.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Then the Seer comes to consciousness in his proper nature.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Heretofore the Seer has been enmeshed in the activities of the psychic nature.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The psychic activities are five; they are either subject or not subject to the five hindrances (Book II, 3).
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These activities are: Sound intellection, unsound intellection, predication, sleep, memory.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The elements of sound intellection are: direct observation, inductive reason, and trustworthy testimony.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Unsound intellection is false understanding, not resting on a perception of the true nature of things.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Predication is carried on through words or thoughts not resting on an object perceived.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Sleep is the psychic condition which rests on mind states, all material things being absent.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Memory is holding to mind-images of things perceived, without modifying them.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The control of these psychic activities comes through the right use of the will, and through ceasing from self-indulgence.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The right use of the will is the steady, effort to stand in spiritual being.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: This becomes a firm resting-place, when followed long, persistently, with earnestness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Ceasing from self-indulgence is conscious mastery over the thirst for sensuous pleasure here or hereafter.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The consummation of this is freedom from thirst for any mode of psychical activity, through the establishment of the spiritual man.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Meditation with an object follows these stages: first, exterior examining, then interior judicial action, then joy, then realization of individual being.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: After the exercise of the will has stilled the psychic activities, meditation rests only on the fruit of former meditations.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Subjective consciousness arising from a natural cause is possessed by those who have laid aside their bodies and been absorbed into subjective nature.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: For the others, there is spiritual consciousness, led up to by faith, valour, right mindfulness, one-pointedness, perception.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Spiritual consciousness is nearest to those of keen, intense will.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The will may be weak, or of middle strength, or intense.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or spiritual consciousness may be gained by ardent service of the Master.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Master is the spiritual man, who is free from hindrances, bondage to works, and the fruition and seed of works.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: In the Master is the perfect seed of Omniscience.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: He is the Teacher of all who have gone before, since he is not limited by Time.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: His word is OM.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Let there be soundless repetition of OM and meditation thereon.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thence come the awakening of interior consciousness, and the removal of barriers.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The barriers to interior consciousness, which drive the psychic nature this way and that, are these: sickness, inertia, doubt, lightmindedness, laziness, intemperance, false notions, inability to reach a stage of meditation, or to hold it when reached.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Grieving, despondency, bodily restlessness, the drawing in and sending forth of the life-breath also contribute to drive the psychic nature to and fro.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Steady application to a principle is the way to put a stop to these.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By sympathy with the happy, compassion for the sorrowful, delight in the holy, disregard of the unholy, the psychic nature moves to gracious peace.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or peace may be reached by the even sending forth and control of the life-breath.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī

translation.text: Faithful, persistent application to any object, if completely attained, will bind the mind to steadiness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: As also will a joyful, radiant spirit.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or the purging of self-indulgence from the psychic nature.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or a pondering on the perceptions gained in dreams and dreamless sleep.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or meditative brooding on what is dearest to the heart.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thus he masters all, from the atom to the Infinite.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā samāpattiḥ

translation.text: When the perturbations of the psychic nature have all been stilled, then the consciousness, like a pure crystal, takes the colour of what it rests on, whether that be the perceiver, perceiving, or the thing perceived.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the consciousness, poised in perceiving, blends together the name, the object dwelt on and the idea, this is perception with exterior consideration.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the object dwells in the mind, clear of memory-pictures, uncoloured by the mind, as a pure luminous idea, this is perception without exterior or consideration.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.devanagari: एतयैव सविचारा निर्विचारा च सूक्ष्मविषया व्याख्याता
passages.iast: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā

translation.text: The same two steps, when referring to things of finer substance, are said to be with, or without, judicial action of the mind.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Subtle substance rises in ascending degrees, to that pure nature which has no distinguishing mark.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The above are the degrees of limited and conditioned spiritual consciousness, still containing the seed of separateness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When pure perception without judicial action of the mind is reached, there follows the gracious peace of the inner self.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: In that peace, perception is unfailingly true.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The object of this perception is other than what is learned from the sacred books, or by sound inference, since this perception is particular.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The impress on the consciousness springing from this perception supersedes all previous impressions.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When this impression ceases, then, since all impressions have ceased, there arises pure spiritual consciousness, with no seed of separateness left.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The practices which make for union with the Soul are: fervent aspiration, spiritual reading, and complete obedience to the Master.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Their aim is, to bring soul-vision, and to wear away hindrances.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These are the hindrances: the darkness of unwisdom, self-assertion, lust hate, attachment.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The darkness of unwisdom is the field of the others. These hindrances may be dormant, or worn thin, or suspended, or expanded.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The darkness of ignorance is: holding that which is unenduring, impure, full of pain, not the Soul, to be eternal, pure, full of joy, the Soul.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Self-assertion comes from thinking of the Seer and the instrument of vision as forming one self.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Lust is the resting in the sense of enjoyment.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Hate is the resting in the sense of pain.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Attachment is the desire toward life, even in the wise, carried forward by its own energy.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These hindrances, when they have become subtle, are to be removed by a countercurrent.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Their active turnings are to be removed by meditation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The burden of bondage to sorrow has its root in these hindrances. It will be felt in this life, or in a life not yet manifested.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From this root there grow and ripen the fruits of birth, of the life-span, of all that is tasted in life.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These bear fruits of rejoicing, or of affliction, as they are sprung from holy or unholy works.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhair guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ

translation.text: To him who possesses discernment, all personal life is misery, because it ever waxes and wanes, is ever afflicted with restlessness, makes ever new dynamic impresses in the mind; and because all its activities war with each other.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: This pain is to be warded off, before it has come.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The cause of what is to be warded off, is the absorption of the Seer in things seen.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Things seen have as their property manifestation, action, inertia. They form the basis of the elements and the sense-powers. They make for experience and for liberation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The grades or layers of the Three Potencies are the defined, the undefined, that with distinctive mark, that without distinctive mark.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Seer is pure vision. Though pure, he looks out through the vesture of the mind.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The very essence of things seen is, that they exist for the Seer.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt

translation.text: Though fallen away from him who has reached the goal, things seen have not alto fallen away, since they still exist for others.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The association of the Seer with things seen is the cause of the realizing of the nature of things seen, and also of the realizing of the nature of the Seer.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The cause of this association is the darkness of unwisdom.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The bringing of this association to an end, by bringing the darkness of unwisdom to an end, is the great liberation; this is the Seer’s attainment of his own pure being.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: A discerning which is carried on without wavering is the means of liberation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: His illuminations is sevenfold, rising In successive stages.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From steadfastly following after the means of Yoga, until impurity is worn away, there comes the illumination of thought up to full discernment.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The eight means of Yoga are: the Commandments, the Rules, right Poise, right Control of the life-force, Withdrawal, Attention, Meditation, Contemplation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Commandments are these: nom injury, truthfulness, abstaining from stealing, from impurity, from covetousness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Commandments, not limited to any race, place, time or occasion, universal, are the great obligation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Rules are these: purity, serenity fervent aspiration, spiritual reading, and per feet obedience to the Master.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When transgressions hinder, the weight of the imagination should be thrown’ on the opposite side.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.devanagari: वितर्का हिंसादयः कृतकारितानुमोदिता लोभक्रोधमोहपूर्वका मृदुमध्याधिमात्रा दुःखाज्ञानानन्तफला इति प्रतिपक्षभावनम्
passages.iast: vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam

translation.text: Transgressions are injury, falsehood, theft, incontinence, envy; whether committed, or caused, or assented to, through greed, wrath, or infatuation; whether faint, or middling, or excessive; bearing endless, fruit of ignorance and pain. Therefore must the weight be cast on the other side.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Where non-injury is perfected, all enmity ceases in the presence of him who possesses it.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When he is perfected in truth, all acts and their fruits depend on him.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Where cessation from theft is perfected, all treasures present themselves to him who possesses it.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: For him who is perfect in continence, the reward is valour and virility.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Where there is firm conquest of covetousness, he who has conquered it awakes to the how and why of life.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through purity a withdrawal from one’s own bodily life, a ceasing from infatuation with the bodily life of others.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: To the pure of heart come also a quiet spirit, one-pointed thought, the victory over sensuality, and fitness to behold the Soul.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From acceptance, the disciple gains happiness supreme.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The perfection of the powers of the bodily vesture comes through the wearing away of impurities, and through fervent aspiration.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through spiritual reading, the disciple gains communion with the divine Power on which his heart is set.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Soul-vision is perfected through perfect obedience to the Master.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Right poise must be firm and without strain.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Right poise is to be gained by steady and temperate effort, and by setting the heart upon the everlasting.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The fruit of right poise is the strength to resist the shocks of infatuation or sorrow.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When this is gained, there follows the right guidance of the life-currents, the control of the incoming and outgoing breath.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The life-current is either outward, or inward, or balanced; it is regulated according to place, time, number; it is prolonged and subtle.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The fourth degree transcends external and internal objects.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereby is worn away the veil which covers up the light.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thence comes the mind’s power to hold itself in the light.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The right Withdrawal is the disengaging of the powers from entanglement in outer things, as the psychic nature has been withdrawn and stilled.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereupon follows perfect mastery over the powers.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The binding of the perceiving consciousness to a certain region is attention (dharana).
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: A prolonged holding of the perceiving consciousness in that region is meditation (dhyana).
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the perceiving consciousness in this meditative is wholly given to illuminating the essential meaning of the object contemplated, and is freed from the sense of separateness and personality, this is contemplation (samadhi).
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When these three, Attention, Meditation Contemplation, are exercised at once, this is perfectly concentrated Meditation (sanyama).
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By mastering this perfectly concentrated Meditation, there comes the illumination of perception.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: This power is distributed in ascending degrees.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: This threefold power, of Attention, Meditation, Contemplation, is more interior than the means of growth previously described.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: But this triad is still exterior to the soul vision which is unconditioned, free from the seed of mental analyses.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: One of the ascending degrees is the development of Control. First there is the overcoming of the mind-impress of excitation. Then comes the manifestation of the mind-impress of Control. Then the perceiving consciousness follows after the moment of Control.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through frequent repetition of this process, the mind becomes habituated to it, and there arises an equable flow of perceiving consciousness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The gradual conquest of the mind’s tendency to flit from one object to another, and the power of one-pointedness, make the development of Contemplation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When, following this, the controlled manifold tendency and the aroused one-pointedness are equally balanced parts of the perceiving consciousness, his the development of one-pointedness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through this, the inherent character, distinctive marks and conditions of being and powers, according to their development, are made clear.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Every object has its characteristics which are already quiescent, those which are active, and those which are not yet definable.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Difference in stage is the cause of difference in development.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through perfectly concentrated Meditation on the three stages of development comes a knowledge of past and future.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The sound and the object and the thought called up by a word are confounded because they are all blurred together in the mind. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the distinction between them, there comes an understanding of the sounds uttered by all beings.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the mind-impressions become visible, there comes an understanding of previous births.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on mind-images is gained the understanding of the thoughts of others.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: But since that on which the thought in the mind of another rests is not objective to the thought-reader’s consciousness, he perceives the thought only, and not also that on which the thought rests.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the form of the body, by arresting the body’s perceptibility, and by inhibiting the eye’s power of sight, there comes the power to make the body invisible.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.devanagari: सोपक्रमं निरुपक्रमं च कर्म तत्संयमादपरान्तज्ञानमरिष्टेभ्यो वा
passages.iast: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamād aparāntajñānam ariṣṭebhyo vā

translation.text: The works which fill out the life-span may be either immediately or gradually operative. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on these comes a knowledge of the time of the end, as also through signs.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on sympathy, compassion and kindness, is gained the power of interior union with others.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on power, even such power as that of the elephant may be gained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By bending upon them the awakened inner light, there comes a knowledge of things subtle, or concealed, or obscure.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the sun comes a knowledge of the worlds.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the moon comes a knowledge of the lunar mansions.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the fixed pole-star comes a knowledge of the motions of the stars.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the lower trunk brings an understanding of the order of the bodily powers.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the well of the throat, there comes the cessation of hunger and thirst.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the channel called the “tortoise-formed,” comes steadfastness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through perfectly concentrated Meditation on the light in the head comes the vision of the Masters who have attained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Or through the divining power of tuition he knows all things.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the heart, the interior being, comes the knowledge of consciousness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthāt svārthasaṃyamāt puruṣajñānam

translation.text: The personal self seeks to feast on life, through a failure to perceive the distinction between the personal self and the spiritual man. All personal experience really exists for the sake of another: namely, the spiritual man. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on experience for the sake of the Self, comes a knowledge of the spiritual man.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereupon are born the divine power of intuition, and the hearing, the touch, the vision, the taste and the power of smell of the spiritual man.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These powers stand in contradistinction to the highest spiritual vision. In manifestation they are called magical powers.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through the weakening of the causes of bondage, and by learning the method of sassing, the consciousness is transferred to the other body.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Through mastery of the upward-life comes freedom from the dangers of water, morass, and thorny places, and the power of ascension is gained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By mastery of the binding-life comes radiance.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From perfectly concentrated Meditation on the correlation of hearing and the ether, comes the power of spiritual hearing.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By perfectly concentrated Meditation em the correlation of the body with the ether, and by thinking of it as light as thistle-down, will come the power to traverse the ether.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ

translation.text: When that condition of consciousness is reached, which is far-reaching and not confined to the body, which is outside the body and not conditioned by it, then the veil which conceals the light is worn away.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Mastery of the elements comes from perfectly concentrated Meditation on their five forms: the gross, the elemental, the subtle, the inherent, the purposive.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereupon will come the manifestation of the atomic and other powers, which are the endowment of the body, together with its unassailable force.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Shapeliness, beauty, force, the temper of the diamond: these are the endowments of that body.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Mastery over the powers of perception and action comes through perfectly concentrated Meditation on their fivefold forms; namely, their power to grasp their distinctive nature, the element of self-consciousness in them, their inherence, and their purposiveness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thence comes the power swift as thought, independent of instruments, and the mastery over matter.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the spiritual man is perfectly disentangled from the psychic body, he attains to mastery over all things and to a knowledge of all.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: By absence of all self-indulgence at this point, when the seeds of bondage to sorrow are destroyed, pure spiritual being is attained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: There should be complete overcoming of allurement or pride in the invitations of the different realms of life, lest attachment to things evil arise once more.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From perfectly concentrated Meditation on the divisions of time and their succession comes that wisdom which is born of discernment.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Hence comes discernment between things which are of like nature, not distinguished by difference of kind, character or position.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam

translation.text: The wisdom which is born of discernment is starlike; it discerns all things, and all conditions of things, it discerns without succession: simultaneously.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the vesture and the spiritual man are alike pure, then perfect spiritual life is attained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Psychic and spiritual powers may be inborn, or they may be gained by the use of drugs, or by incantations, or by fervour, or by Meditation.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The transfer of powers from one venture to another comes through the flow of the natural creative forces.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat

translation.text: The apparent, immediate cause is not the true cause of the creative nature-powers; but, like the husbandman in his field, it takes obstacles away.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Vestures of consciousness are built up in conformity with the Boston of the feeling of selfhood.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: In the different fields of manifestation, the Consciousness, though one, is the elective cause of many states of consciousness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Among states of consciousness, that which is born of Contemplation is free from the seed of future sorrow.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The works of followers after Union make neither for bright pleasure nor for dark pain The works of others make for pleasure or pain, or a mingling of these.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: From the force inherent in works comes the manifestation of those dynamic mind images which are conformable to the ripening out of each of these works.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Works separated by different nature, or place, or time, are brought together by the correspondence between memory and dynamic impression.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The series of dynamic mind-images is beginningless, because Desire is everlasting.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Since the dynamic mind-images are held together by impulses of desire, by the wish for personal reward, by the substratum of mental habit, by the support of outer things desired; therefore, when these cease, the self reproduction of dynamic mind-images ceases.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The difference between that which is past and that which is not yet come, according to their natures, depends on the difference of phase of their properties.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These properties, whether manifest or latent, are of the nature of the Three Potencies.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The external manifestation of an object takes place when the transformations ore in the same phase.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The paths of material things and of states of consciousness are distinct, as is manifest from the fact that the same object may produce different impressions in different minds.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.devanagari: न चैकचित्ततन्त्रं वस्तु तदप्रमाणकं तदा किं स्यात्
passages.iast: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt

translation.text: Nor do material objects depend upon a single mind, for how could they remain objective to others, if that mind ceased to think of them?
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: An object is perceived, or not perceived, according as the mind is, or is not, tinged with the colour of the object.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The movements of the psychic nature are perpetually objects of perception, since the Spiritual Man, who is the lord of them, remains unchanging.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The Mind is not self-luminous, since it can be seen as an object.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Nor could the Mind at the same time know itself and things external to it.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: If the Mind be thought of as seen by another more inward Mind, then there would be an endless series of perceiving Minds, and a confusion of memories.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When the psychical nature takes on the form of the spiritual intelligence, by reflecting it, then the Self becomes conscious of its own spiritual intelligence.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The psychic nature, taking on the colour of the Seer and of things seen, leads to the perception of all objects.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: tad asaṃkhyeyavāsanābhiś citram api parārthaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt

translation.text: The psychic nature, which has been printed with mind-images of innumerable material things, exists now for the Spiritual Man, building for him.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: For him who discerns between the Mind and the Spiritual Man, there comes perfect fruition of the longing after the real being of the Self.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereafter, the whole personal being bends toward illumination, toward Eternal Life.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: In the internals of the batik, other thoughts will arise, through the impressions of the dynamic mind-images.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: These are to be overcome as it was taught that hindrances should be overcome.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.iast: prasaṃkhyāne 'py akusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāter dharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ

translation.text: He who, after he has attained, is wholly free from self, reaches the essence of all that can be known, gathered together like a cloud. This is the true spiritual consciousness.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereon comes surcease from sorrow and the burden of toil.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: When all veils are rent, all stains washed away, his knowledge becomes infinite; little remains for him to know.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: Thereafter comes the completion of the series of transformations of the three nature potencies, since their purpose is attained.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

translation.text: The series of transformations is divided into moments. When the series is completed, time gives place to duration.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man

passages.devanagari: पुरुषार्थशून्यानां गुणानां प्रतिप्रसवः कैवल्यं स्वरूपप्रतिष्ठा वा चितिशक्तिरिति
passages.iast: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti

translation.text: Pure spiritual life is, therefore, the inverse resolution of the potencies of Nature, which have emptied themselves of their value for the Spiritual man; or it is the return of the power of pure Consciousness to its essential form.
translation.author: Charles Johnston
translation.work: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Book of the Spiritual Man
